records.rationale: The derivation is correct with its stated roughly constant load current and small-ripple approximation. Full-wave peaks repeat at twice the input AC frequency; capacitor discharge over approximately 1/(2f) gives peak-to-peak ripple I/(2fC). The answer explicitly labels the result approximate.

evidence.finding: DeltaV=DeltaQ/C=I*DeltaT/C with DeltaT≈1/(2f). Units A/(s^-1*F)=V. At I=0.1 A, f=50 Hz and C=0.001 F, the approximation gives 1 V peak-to-peak.

records.rationale: Loss of seal recovery can contribute to leakage and subsequent corrosion, but the answer presents the entire failure chain as inevitable once compression set is permanent. Hold the unqualified causal chain rather than silently adding those conditions.

evidence.title: Parker O-Ring Handbook ORD5700, section2.4.11

records.rationale: For ordinary voltage-driven capacitor charging, added series resistance limits the initial current and lengthens charging time; the resistor dissipates heat during charging. evidence.finding: For an ideal voltage step, I(0+)=(Vs-Vc0)/Rtotal and tau=Rtotal*C. Increasing positive Rtotal reduces initial current and increases tau. P_R=I²R during charging; total ideal charge-event loss must not be inferred to grow with R.

records.rationale: Appropriate Weibull-analysis workflow includes defined failure criteria, censored units, failure-mode separation, parameter estimation, fit assessment and engineering validation. Beta is described as suggesting hazard behavior rather than proving a failure mechanism. No unsupported life metric or confidence bound is computed.

evidence.title: NIST Weibull Plot guidance
evidence.finding: Weibull analysis checks distributional assumptions and estimates shape/scale; appropriate plotting methods can handle censored data.

For a two-parameter Weibull, hazard h(t)=(beta/eta)*(t/eta)^(beta-1): decreasing for beta<1, constant for beta=1 and increasing for beta>1. That supports the qualitative interpretation while fit validity remains necessary.
